findings.explanation: The PR adds workspace__slug and project_id filters to the Issue.objects query on line 1121, which properly scopes the bulk update to the authorized project. However, the @allow_permission decorator on line 1113 only validates that the user has ADMIN or MEMBER role in the project, but does NOT verify that the issue IDs provided in request.data actually belong to the workspace and project being updated. A user could bypass the scope by directly manipulating issue_ids in the request to reference issues from other projects. The filter ensures the query only fetches issues from the current project/workspace, but there is no validation that the user-supplied issue_ids should have been restricted to begin with - they are accepted blindly from request.data and only filtered after fetch.

evidence.content: Issue.objects applies automatic filtering for archived, draft, and triage issues, while Issue.objects has no filtering by workspace/project scope - showing why explicit scope filters are necessary

findings.suggested_fix: Validate that all issue_ids provided in request.data belong to the specified workspace and project before processing. The current approach filters the results, but an attacker could submit issue IDs from other projects knowing they will be silently ignored. Add validation: ensure len(issue_ids) == len(issues) to detect when requested issues are outside the allowed scope, or pre-validate issue_ids against the workspace/project.
